claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a coherent ordered L12 precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high-entropy alloy is a single intervention applicable to Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Low-temperature annealing of Al0.7CoCrFeNi causes ordered L12 precipitates to form within the fcc phase.
The effective low-temperature annealing range is 500–700 °C.
Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a lamellar dual-phase fcc + B2 microstructure.
The lamellar fcc + B2 microstructure is the structural mediator created by the stated intervention.
The L12 precipitates are coherent and nanoscale.
Fine L12 precipitates strengthen Al0.7CoCrFeNi through Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass.
Formation of coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates is itself experimental evidence that Orowan bypass is the operative mechanism.
The intervention will increase yield strength by at least 10% relative to untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by at least 5% relative to untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The predicted improvement should hold under quasi-static loading at 10^-3 s^-1 and dynamic loading at 10^3 s^-1.
The effect of the intervention on strain-rate sensitivity is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as introducing a precipitation-strengthenable eutectic alloy, whereas the conditions and evidence imply that the actionable intervention is low-temperature annealing of the existing Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy to precipitate L12.

The structural mediator is specified as the pre-existing lamellar fcc + B2 microstructure, but the stated mechanism is attributed to annealing-induced L12 precipitates; the hypothesis does not connect the listed mediator to the mechanism.
